title: Hair transplant in Istanbul — what actually happens, step by step
desc:
No marketing language. Just an honest account of the process from the moment you reach out to the moment your result is complete.

1
Before anything

You reach out on WhatsApp
No forms, no waiting room. The first contact happens on WhatsApp — you send a few photos of your scalp (front, top, back, and donor area) and the team assesses your case.

What you'll hear back is honest: how many grafts you realistically need, which technique suits your situation, and whether you're a good candidate at all. If you're not ready for a transplant, they'll tell you that too.

What to send

Good lighting, hair dry, no filters. Photos taken from the front, crown, and back. The better the photos, the more accurate the initial assessment.

2
Planning your trip

You book — and we handle the rest
Once you confirm, the package covers airport transfer, 2 nights hotel accommodation, and all clinic visits. You arrive in Istanbul, get picked up, and check in. Simple.

Plan for 3–4 days in total. The procedure itself is one day, but you'll want a day before and a day after to settle and recover before flying home.

Included in the package

Airport pickup and drop-off

2 nights hotel

All clinic transfers

Post-op care kit

3
Day 1 — arrival

In-person consultation at the clinic
You don't go straight into surgery. The first day is entirely for consultation — your surgeon examines your donor area in person, assesses density, and designs your hairline with you in front of a mirror.

This is the most important conversation of the whole process. Ask everything you've been wondering. The hairline doesn't get drawn until you're both happy with it.

Good questions to ask

How many grafts are we placing, and where exactly?

What does my donor area look like — any limitations?

Which technique do you recommend for my case, and why?

4
Day 2 — the procedure

FUE or DHI — which one and why it matters
The technique isn't chosen at random — it depends on your hair type, scalp condition, and what you're trying to achieve. Both involve extracting individual follicular units from the donor area and placing them where they're needed. The difference is in how placement happens.

FUE

Follicles are extracted, then channels are opened in the recipient area before placement. Gives the surgeon more control over angle and direction across larger areas.

DHI

Extraction and placement happen in one step using a Choi pen. No channels needed — less handling of grafts, higher precision. Often preferred for the hairline and density work.

On the day

The procedure takes 6–8 hours depending on graft count. Local anaesthetic is used — it's not painful. You'll be lying down for most of it. There are breaks. Bring headphones.

The anaesthetic injections at the start are the most uncomfortable part. After that, most people doze off.

5
After the procedure

Recovery — the honest timeline
This part is where most people aren't prepared. The first wash is done at the clinic the morning after. You'll be shown exactly how to wash and care for your scalp for the first two weeks — it matters a lot.

Then you fly home. And then the waiting begins.

What to expect, month by month

Days 1–14
Redness, scabbing, sensitivity. Normal. Keep the area clean and avoid touching it.
Weeks 2–6
The transplanted hairs shed. This is called shock loss and it looks alarming. It is completely normal — the follicles are resting, not dying.
Month 3–4
Slow regrowth begins. Still thin and patchy at this point. Hard to judge anything yet.
Month 6
You can see something real. Most patients start feeling positive around here.
Month 12–18
Final result. Full thickness, full density. This is what you actually came for.

The hardest part

Month 2 and 3 are psychologically the toughest. Your hair looks worse than before the procedure. This is temporary — but knowing it and experiencing it are two different things. The Lucera team stays reachable on WhatsApp throughout. If something doesn't look right or you're worried, you message them.

One last thing

A hair transplant is a permanent procedure. The grafts that take are yours for life. But not every follicle will take — no honest clinic will tell you 100% will. A good result is typically 85–95% graft survival, achieved over 12–18 months.

Anyone who promises instant perfection is selling something. Anyone who walks you through the full picture — including the difficult months — is someone worth trusting with this.
